title: Comparison of sodium hydroxide and alkaline hypochlorite cleaning protocols for ultrafiltration membranes fouled with dairy process streams

record.title: Comparison of sodium hydroxide and alkaline hypochlorite cleaning protocols for ultrafiltration membranes fouled with dairy process streams
record.abstract: Three laboratory-scale cleaning protocols were evaluated for polyethersulphone and ceramic ultrafiltration membranes fouled with skim milk and cottage cheese whey streams. Protocol A used 0.5% NaOH at 50 °C for 30 min; Protocol B used 200 ppm NaOCl followed by 0.5% NaOH at 40 °C; Protocol C used 0.3% NaOH with 0.1% sodium dodecyl sulphate at 45 °C. Hydraulic cleaning efficiency was assessed by pure water flux recovery (PWFR) and irreversible fouling resistance. Protocol B achieved the highest PWFR of 97.4% for polyethersulphone membranes but reduced membrane lifetime by approximately 18% after 30 cleaning cycles, as indicated by contact angle measurements and SEM analysis. Protocol C preserved membrane integrity better and achieved PWFR of 93.1%. Ceramic membranes showed consistently higher PWFR across all protocols (>98%). The results inform CIP cycle design for dairy ultrafiltration plant operations.
